headline: Student stabbed and robbed on moving train roof in Dhaka's Mohakhali area
summary: A civil engineering student was attacked by a group of muggers who stole his phone and wallet after stabbing him multiple times. He is currently receiving treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital.
details: A 22-year-old civil engineering student, Hasanuzzaman Sajid, was stabbed and robbed by a group of muggers on the roof of a moving train in Dhaka's Mohakhali area. The incident occurred on Monday night around 7:30 PM on the Brahmaputra Express, which was traveling from Kamalapur to Jamalpur.

Sajid, a student of Bangladesh Army University of Engineering and Technology (BAUE&T) in Qadirabad, Natore, was returning to his village home in Jamalpur. He boarded the train's roof from Kamalapur station.

According to Sajid and his uncle, Shahidur Rahman, a group of seven to eight individuals surrounded him near Mohakhali. They then stabbed him in his hands, chest, back, and left leg before taking his mobile phone and wallet, which he claims contained Tk 8,500.

Locals and Railway Police Constable Md Rubel Pramanik from the Airport Police Outpost rescued the injured student near the Airport Railway Station. He was initially taken to Kurmitola General Hospital.

Later, around 10 PM, Sajid was transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for advanced treatment. Inspector Md Habibur Rahman, in-charge of the DMCH Police Camp, confirmed that the student is receiving emergency care and the relevant railway police station has been informed.

headline: UAE cancels visas for over 4,000 Bangladeshis, leaving many stranded without explanation
summary: Over 4,000 Bangladeshi expatriates are now unable to return to their jobs and businesses in the UAE after their visas were abruptly cancelled, with no reasons provided. The Bangladesh government is engaging diplomatically to resolve the crisis.
details: The United Arab Emirates has cancelled the visas of over 4,000 Bangladeshis, leaving many stranded at home after returning on leave. No explanation has been provided as to why they can no longer return to their jobs and businesses.

The Bangladesh government has raised the issue with the UAE through diplomatic channels, seeking a review of the cancellations. Affected Bangladeshis have given authorities until September 22 to find a solution.

Abul Kalam Azad, who lived in the UAE for 27 years, returned to Bangladesh on April 7 and received an email on July 24 informing him of his visa cancellation without reason. He was among 350 affected individuals demanding a solution at a Jatiya Press Club event.

State Minister for Expatriates’ Welfare Nurul Haque Nur confirmed on Facebook that his ministry and the foreign ministry are aware of the cancellations, with the number later rising to 4,800. Efforts are underway to resolve the matter diplomatically.

Affected expatriates have placed a five-point demand, including rehabilitation and financial assistance of Tk 15,000-20,000 monthly until the crisis is resolved. They also urged the government to arrange employment in other countries if returning to the UAE is not possible.

MS Shekil Chowdhury, chairperson of Centre for Non-Resident Bangladeshi, noted increased scrutiny by the UAE amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. He suggested factors like visa renewals, document problems, social media activity, and potential security concerns are being examined more closely, though not directly linked to the cancellations.
